OVERVIEW The Elder Scrolls Online: Tamriel Unlimited v2.0.13 is an incremental patch for PC/Mac that fixes a few issues with quests, crafting, and gameplay. We are also updating the Terms of Service, which you will be prompted to accept upon login. The size of this patch is 134MB.

FIXES & IMPROVEMENTS

Combat & Gameplay

Champion System

The Ritual

Last Stand: Fixed an issue where this passive was not correctly granting Ultimate when triggered.

Crafting & Economy

General

Fixed an issue where guild traders were not displaying the hiring guild's name or heraldry immediately after being hired.

Alchemy

Potions of Weapon Power now have the same 45 second cooldown as all other potions.

Crown Store

General

Fixed an issue where the Crown Tri-Restoration Potion was not providing the Major Fortitude buff when consumed.

Dungeons & Group Content

Dungeons

Direfrost Keep

Nobles’ Rest: You can now obtain this quest until you reach the Great Hall.

Quests & Zones

Deshaan

School Daze: Clarified the map and compass pins for the step to Assist Teldras. After you speak with him the first time, the pins will now properly move to the nearby book and the pond itself instead of over Teldras.

Eastmarch

One Victor, One King: Your quest progress will no longer become blocked in the event Leimaer or any of the Stormfist warriors get stuck.

Reaper’s March

The Moonlit Path: You will now consistently be able to complete the event “Defend the Silvenar and the Green Lady.”

The Rift

Pulled Under: You will no longer block other player characters from investigating the dead Worm Cult Assassin if you are already interacting with it.

I'm planning on getting my husband a new board game for our wedding anniversary but I'm having some trouble deciding what game to buy, so I was hoping to get some suggestions of fun game he might like based on what he currently plays.

Games he enjoys include:

  • Dominion - We have all expansions expect for Adventures, which I'm getting him already.

  • Settlers of Catan

  • Puerto Rico

  • Agricola

  • Battlestar Galactica - This is my favorite

  • 7 Wonders - We have the cities and leaders expansions

  • Pandemic

  • Love Letter

  • Mansions of Madness - We have it, but haven't played it yet.

We usually play games just the two of us or with friends, rarely no more than 4. When it comes to play time we're really open as long as the game is fun. He tends to like games that are more strategy based as opposed to luck as well. I've thought about getting Twilight Struggle since it's so popular on BGG but I'm a little worried about it only being 2 players. I was also thinking about Terra Mystica. The budget is really open as well.

Thanks for any suggestions!

Ticket to Ride is a good one. Like Settlers of Catan you can either be nice or you can ruin someone's night instead.

Your choice!
Thanks! Ticket to Ride has been on my short list for ideas.

Of course if you like card games and tequila there's always Cards Against Humanity. Best played with more than 2 people.

Tequila optional

We have CAH. I just completely forgot to include it in my list.

We tend to play with beer though since I'm not much of a tequila person. Thanks though!
Eah. I'd recommend against it. If your above list is anything to go off of, TTR's strategy is too far on the light side of things.

If you/he like smaller games (Love Letter) and card drafting (7 Wonders) Sushi Go may be right up your alley. Forbidden Island/Desert make for some interesting and inexpensive co-ops along the same lines as Pandemic. San Juan is a role selection card game that emulates a bit of the euro-ness of Puerto Rico in a nice, compact card game that's a lot of fun.

If you both like Dominion, Star Realms is an inexpensive and excellent deck builder for 2 people. At least, it's inexpensive until you spend more money on all the expansions. :)

Dominion is his favorite so I'll definitely be checking out Star Realms.

Thanks for the suggestions!
If you like Battlestar, and don't mind the zombie theme, Dead of Winter is great. Based on your games listed Caverna is probably a good bet too.
Dead of Winter looks really good. I'm a big fan of co-op games. I'll be sure to look up Caverna as well. Thanks!

Castles of Burgundy.

I'd say that has similarities to both Puerto Rico and Settlers of Catan. I rate it slightly higher than Puerto Rico in my stable of games now. Its also great with smaller numbers. I've only played 3 player myself so far, but it handles 2-4 and I think 2 would be just as fun as 3.
Thanks! I've had other people suggest this game too. It looks interesting.
Munchkin, part luck and strategy but mostly strategy. Lots of fuckery against other players and the ability to team up. Oh, and loooooooads of expansions.

We played Munchkin once and he absolutely hated it, but I really think it was more about that particular situation than the actual game. I'm going to have to convince him to play it again sometime so we can see what the game is actually like.

Munchkin is incredibly fun, but super easy. Makes it great for big gatherings when nobody wants to learn rules, or most of the participants are drunk.

Steve Jackson does great nerd fan service in the games. Just know that the challenge fades quickly since they're more about the luck of the draw than strategy.

Twilight Struggle is high ranking but it's very heavy. Meaning few are willing to put in the time to learn the game but those that do love it. I played it once didn't enjoy it, it's one if those game where you'll hate it the frist few plays of it.

Games I enjoy at 2 that scales well to 4 are: Five Tribes- Easy- Worker replacement game? Lots of fun. Scoville- Easy- pepper farmer game very under rated. Splendor- Easy- engine building game Ticket to Ride is a great intro game

Telsa vs Edison is a new game coming out its amazing. Great stock market mechanic.

Keyflower-Medium- a greay game one of my favorites, a lot going on in this game can be overwhelming at first.

Be sure to check out reviews of these games on YouTube don't rely on BGG rating ever play group has it's own flavor.
I'll definitely have to look at Telsa v. Edison. His studied economics in undergrad and would probably love something like that. Thanks for the suggestions.
Alhambra, is the halfway point between the tile laying of Carcassonne and the resource management of Settlers. It's one of the Big Four European style board games and a must have on your shelf.
